inputs.net_debt_basis: bank borrowings 71.564 - cash 2.823 + NCI book value 0.596 (Cibus 49% minority). IFRS-16 lease liabilities (141.512) are EXCLUDED from net debt because the full lease cash cost (principal + interest, 4.7% of FY2026 revenue) is charged inside the flows as lease_cost_pct - lease treatment (B), leases as operating cost, charged exactly once.
inputs.owner_fcf_bridge: last_fcf = reported FCF 9.048 + bank interest paid 4.558 (added back: model is unlevered, bank debt charged once in the net-debt bridge; RAD presents interest paid inside OPERATING cash flow) - lease principal 2.830 (in financing, moved into the flows) - SBC 0.380 - interest income 0.061 = 10.335. Lease INTEREST 6.898 is already deducted inside reported OCF and stays deducted - it is NOT re-deducted (that would double-count) and NOT added back.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2026 annual report, share-based payments 380k (LTIP); near-SBC-zero market
inputs.share_count_basis: 283.862m ordinary shares at FY2026 balance date (31-Mar-2026), held FLAT; SBC fully expensed so diluting as well would double-charge. Trivial LTIP dilution. 14:1 share split 8-Dec-2020 means FY2019/FY2020 raw counts (12.5m) are pre-split - split-adjusted 175m.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-08-27T04:09:24Z (16:09 NZST, regular session; verified vs task anchor 0.465)
inputs.wacc_rationale: Built additively in NZD per the Step 8c.5 NZ small-cap template: NZ 10-yr risk-free ~4.4% + equity risk premium ~4.6% = 9.0% base cost of capital; + 2.0% small-cap illiquidity (market cap ~NZ$132m < NZ$300m, thin NZX turnover, founder-concentrated register); + 2.0% single-payer concentration (~87% of revenue is the Health NZ / WINZ / ACC bed-day rate - the government sets the price, a regulatory single point of failure); + 1.5% financial leverage (bank + lease obligations NZ$213m vs NZ$76m equity; covenants complied with but headroom is thin for a price-taker). WACC = 14.5%, same for all three scenarios (risk is charged once, in the discount rate for structural risks and in scenario weights for event outcomes - never per-scenario WACCs).
notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF (dcf-methods SKILL routing: operating company - government-funded aged-care fees, not a NAV vehicle, not a REIT (no material ORA/DMF village economics: refundable ORA liability only 38.9m and village fees ~1% of revenue), not a bank). 10-year explicit horizon, component-built margins, scenario-weighted. Fresh build - no prior RAD.NZ DCF.

LEASES are the central adjustment: ~half of the 25 care homes are leasehold. FY2026 total_debt 213.1 = 71.6 bank + 141.5 IFRS-16 leases. Treatment (B): full lease cash cost inside the flows (lease_cost_pct 4.8% of revenue = FY2026 principal 2.830 + interest 6.898 = 9.728 on revenue 205.5), lease liabilities excluded from net debt. Precedents: MOV.NZ, TPW.AX, 2CC.NZ, 3116.T.

RAD presents bank interest AND lease interest inside operating cash flow (FY2026 statement of cash flows), so reported OCF 25.121 is already post-both; only lease principal sits in financing. The owner-FCF bridge reflects this - see owner_fcf_bridge.

D&A driver (3.7%) is OWNED-asset D&A only (FY2026: total 13.206 - ROU depreciation 5.604 = 7.602). ROU depreciation is excluded because the cash lease cost is already charged; including it would double-charge leases in the tax build.
CASH TAX ramps 18% -> 28% NZ statutory over 5 years. FY2026 cash tax paid 3.496 = ~16% of model EBIT 21.4 (carryforwards/timing); assuming the low rate persists would overstate value.

CAPEX 3.0% of revenue (base) is normalized maintenance + modest owned development. FY2026 reported capex 16.073 (7.8%) was acquisition-heavy (St Allisa business acquisition 14.7, largely recycled via a 13.65m sale-and-leaseback to a related party); FY2024-25 ran 2.4-3.5%. Growth beds are deliberately third-party funded (capital-light) - their cost appears in lease_cost_pct, not capex.
NCI: Cibus catering is 51%-owned; NCI book value 0.596 added to the net-debt bridge (NCI profit share ~0.2m/yr, immaterial to flows).
WORKING CAPITAL: 8% capture on the CHANGE in revenue (FY2026 payables +2.679 and net refundable-ORA inflow +1.063 on Δrevenue +24.9 = ~15% actual; modelled conservatively at 8%).
INTEREST INCOME 0.061 stripped for formula consistency; trivial (company is net-debt).

FY2019/FY2020 filings are OCR'd scans (low confidence) and FY2020 is the IFRS-16 adoption year; history for trend-fitting starts FY2021. FY2021 owner FCF also excludes an 8.823m lease-interest year already inside OCF.
Aug-2026 Ministerial Advisory Group ~7.1% aged-care price-uplift recommendation is a RECOMMENDATION, not enacted funding: it drives the BULL case, not the base.

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGRs are unusable as the primary anchor: the 5yr figure (25.9%) is distorted by the FY2022 capital raise (equity 24.1 -> 70.1) and the 3yr figure (1.6%) by FY2023/FY2024 impairment losses. EPS 5yr (28.0%, split-adjusted cents) is a loss-to-recovery artefact. Owner-FCF CAGR (15.9% 5yr) spans two hugely negative acquisition-capex years (FY2022 -31.5, FY2023 -50.9) - the series is presented for audit, not trend-fitting. Revenue CAGR (10.3% 5yr, 11.1% 3yr) is the only clean series; base year-1 growth is set below it (9%) and decelerates to 2.5%.

scenario_narratives.base: Government bed-day rate keeps rising at roughly wage-inflation pass-through (annual ARRC uplifts of 3-4%) but the MAG 7.1% catalyst is NOT enacted; occupancy holds 95-96% against a 94.9% FY2026 actual; Karori annualises in FY2027 (year-1 growth 9%) and the capital-light leasehold pipeline adds beds slowly, decelerating revenue growth to 2.5% by year 10. EBITDA margin drifts 19.2% -> 20.5% as occupancy and Cibus/Home Support scale slightly outpace wage inflation. Cash tax normalises to 28%.
scenario_narratives.bull: The MAG-recommended ~7.1% price uplift is enacted in Budget 2027 (year-2 growth 11%) on top of demographic demand (9,000+ bed national shortfall by late 2030s); occupancy reaches management's 97-98% target; the 20-home capital-light pipeline executes; adjacent revenue (Cibus, Home Support, Luma) compounds. Margin reaches 22.0% - sector-leading EBITDAR per bed extends.
scenario_narratives.bear: A fiscally constrained government freezes or under-indexes the bed-day rate while minimum-wage and AEWV-driven labour costs keep rising 5-6%: revenue growth falls to 1-3% and EBITDA margin compresses 19% -> 16% (roughly the FY2024 level). The leveraged, leasehold-heavy structure (fixed lease + bank charges ~14m/yr) makes thin margins painful; dividend is cut; no covenant breach is assumed but headroom narrows. Terminal growth 1%, terminal cap 10x.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear 20% (up from the 15% house default): single-payer rate-setting plus 213m of fixed lease+bank obligations against 76m equity means a funding freeze bites hard - but covenant compliance is confirmed, ASB facilities extend to June 2028, and demand is demographically underwritten, so going-concern stress is not the central case. Bull 30% (down from 35%): the MAG 7.1% uplift is a genuine live catalyst but requires Budget appropriation - one government decision, not yet made. Structural risks (payer concentration, illiquidity, leverage) are charged in the 14.5% WACC, not double-charged in the weights.

valuation_philosophy: Radius is valued as an operating company on unlevered owner FCF with the full IFRS-16 lease cash cost (principal + interest, ~4.8% of revenue) charged inside the flows and only bank net debt (+NCI) deducted - charging the 141.5m lease liability as debt as well would double-count roughly half the enterprise. The 14.5% WACC is deliberately punitive versus a generic 9-10%: it prices small-cap NZX illiquidity (+2.0%), the ~87% single-payer government rate-setting dependency (+2.0%) and high leverage (+1.5%) on top of a 9.0% NZ base rate. On those terms the FY2026 operating momentum (revenue +13.8%, EBITDA 39.1m, NPAT +36%, occupancy 94.9% and rising, dividend +50%, clean audit, covenants met) is roughly fully priced at $0.465: base IV $0.46 (-1%), weighted IV $0.45 (-3%). The stock is NOT a mispricing at the current price on house assumptions - it is a fair-value hold whose upside case (IV $0.61, +32%) rests on the government enacting the Aug-2026 MAG ~7.1% price uplift, and whose bear case (IV $0.18, -61%) shows how hard a funding freeze hits a leveraged price-taker. Implied base multiples (13.5x adjusted P/E, 5.2x EV/EBITDA, 1.7x P/B) sit inside the company's own trading history - the sanity check passed with no fix required.
